SECTION 01

Platform Overview & Mission

OrcaWolf AI is an architecture demonstrator for sovereign, AI-native Electronic Health Record (EHR) infrastructure — built to show what is possible when zero-trust networking, cryptographic identity, and clinical AI are designed as a unified system from the ground up.

Healthcare data is among the most sensitive information that exists. Yet most EHR infrastructure was designed before the internet became adversarial, before AI was a first-class clinical participant, and long before regulators demanded cryptographic proof of data lineage. OrcaWolf AI exists to close that gap — demonstrating a complete reference architecture that is sovereign, resilient, and verifiable at every layer.

The platform serves three communities simultaneously:

  • Defence medical planners — through naval carrier readiness simulation, mass casualty triage modeling, and C2 dashboard telemetry
  • Healthcare technology architects — through a detailed six-layer sovereign mesh reference architecture with interactive 3D visualizations
  • AI and cloud engineers — through Vertex AI vector pipeline integration, FHIR R4 bundle generation, and load testing simulation

1.1 The OrcaWolf Name

The name reflects the architecture's character. The orca represents disciplined, coordinated pack intelligence — highly organised, mission-focused, operating as a unified system. The wolf represents zero-trust instinct — nothing passes without being vouched for. Together they describe a system that is both intelligent and uncompromising in its security posture.

SECTION 02

Home Page — Technology Pillars Explained

The six pillars on the OrcaWolf AI home page represent the foundational technology decisions that underpin the entire sovereign mesh architecture. Each is a deliberate design choice, not a product feature.

2.1 Zero-Trust mTLS

What it means: Mutual Transport Layer Security (mTLS) requires both sides of every network connection to prove their identity using cryptographic certificates before any data is exchanged. Unlike standard TLS — where only the server proves its identity to the client — mTLS eliminates the concept of implicit internal trust entirely.

Why it matters for EHR: Traditional hospital networks assume that anything inside the firewall is trustworthy. A single compromised workstation can then move laterally to reach every patient record. mTLS means a compromised pod cannot communicate with any other service without a valid, recently-issued certificate — and that certificate is cryptographically bound to a specific workload identity, not a shared secret or password.

How it works in OrcaWolf AI: Certificate rotation is automatic and happens every few hours via cert-manager integrated with the SPIRE identity server. No human ever touches a private key in production. If a service's certificate expires or is revoked, it immediately loses the ability to communicate — zero administrative action required.

2.2 Ambient Mesh / ztunnel

What it means: Istio Ambient Mesh is a next-generation service mesh architecture that removes the requirement for a sidecar proxy in every pod. Instead, a single ztunnel (zero-trust tunnel) agent runs on each Kubernetes node and handles all inter-pod traffic transparently.

Why it matters: Traditional sidecar meshes add 15–30% memory overhead per pod and require pod restarts to update mesh configuration. At the scale of a hospital EHR system — potentially thousands of pods — this becomes operationally untenable. Ambient Mesh reduces mesh overhead by up to 70% while maintaining identical security guarantees.

HBONE tunneling: All traffic between nodes flows through HBONE (HTTP-Based Overlay Network Encapsulation) tunnels — encrypted, authenticated, and policy-enforced at the kernel level before any application code runs.

2.3 Mass Casualty Simulation

What it means: The MCI Simulation module provides a configurable, AI-driven triage and resource allocation engine for Mass Casualty Incidents. Casualty distributions, resource consumption, and event timelines are generated using probability weights derived from published military medical doctrine.

Underlying standards: NATO STANAG 2122 casualty estimation tables, US Joint Trauma System Clinical Practice Guidelines (JTS CPG), and TCCC (Tactical Combat Casualty Care) field statistics.

FHIR R4 output: Every simulation run generates a fully-formed FHIR R4 Bundle — real clinical resources (Patient, Condition, Observation) in the format required by modern health information exchanges. These bundles can be fed directly into production ingestion pipelines.

2.4 Google AI Suite

What it means: The platform integrates Vertex AI (Google's managed ML platform), BigQuery (petabyte-scale analytics), Gemini (Google's frontier reasoning model), and Cloud Healthcare API — all operating within the sovereign mesh perimeter.

Key capability — Vertex AI text-embedding-004: Clinical text summaries from FHIR resources are converted to 768-dimensional semantic vectors using Google's text embedding model. These vectors enable cosine similarity search — finding the most clinically relevant past cases for a given presentation without exposing raw PHI.

Sovereign boundary: All AI inference calls remain within VPC-SC perimeters. The AI never receives raw PHI — only de-identified or synthetic clinical summaries.

2.5 Sovereign Data

What it means: Every patient record in the OrcaWolf AI architecture is encrypted with Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) held in Cloud KMS — not by Google, not by a third party, but by the owning organisation. Data residency is guaranteed by VPC Service Controls that prevent exfiltration even if a cloud identity is compromised.

Provenance ledger: Every read, write, transform, and export event is recorded in an immutable audit chain, with each entry signed by the workload's cryptographic identity. This satisfies HIPAA audit requirements natively — no bolted-on compliance tools required.

2.6 EHR Interop Layer

What it means: The interoperability layer bridges the two dominant healthcare data standards — FHIR R4 (the modern REST-based standard) and HL7 v2.x (the legacy message-based standard still used by 90% of hospitals worldwide) — without requiring either side to change.

US Core Implementation Guide: All FHIR resources are profiled against US Core IG to ensure compatibility with US healthcare information exchanges and federal reporting requirements.

De-identification pipeline: Before any data reaches an AI workload, it passes through the Cloud Healthcare API de-identification engine, producing Safe Harbor or Expert Determination compliant datasets automatically.

SECTION 03

Architecture — The Six-Layer Sovereign Stack

The OrcaWolf AI architecture is organised as a six-layer trust hierarchy — L0 through L5 — where each layer derives its security guarantees from the layer below it. Trust is never assumed; it is always cryptographically proven and flows upward from hardware.

ℹ
Interactive Walkthrough Available

The Architecture page on the site includes a layer-by-layer interactive walkthrough with 3D visualisations. Click "Start Layer-by-Layer Walkthrough" to explore each layer in detail with animated trust-flow indicators.

L0

Physical / Cloud Substrate

INFRASTRUCTURE ANCHOR

The foundation of the entire sovereign mesh begins at the physical and cloud infrastructure layer — where hardware meets policy. OrcaWolf AI runs on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) Autopilot clusters provisioned with Confidential Computing nodes, meaning the CPU itself encrypts data in use — not just at rest or in transit. Even the cloud provider cannot read workload memory.

Every storage volume is encrypted using Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) held in Cloud KMS, giving the organisation — not Google — the authority to revoke access instantly. VPC Service Controls wrap the entire environment in a logical perimeter that prevents data exfiltration even if an identity is compromised inside the cluster.

Every node in the cluster attests its integrity through Shielded VM measured boot, and the resulting attestation is fed into the SPIRE trust root at L2. The physical layer is the anchor; every higher layer derives its trustworthiness from what is established here.

GKE Autopilot Confidential VMs Cloud KMS (CMEK) VPC-SC Perimeter Shielded VM Boot Workload Identity Federation
L1

Ambient Mesh / ztunnel

MESH FABRIC

Istio Ambient Mesh eliminates sidecars entirely by moving L4 policy enforcement to a per-node ztunnel agent. The ztunnel runs as a DaemonSet — one instance per node — and handles all inter-pod communication using HBONE (HTTP-Based Overlay Network Encapsulation) tunneling. Every packet between pods traverses this encrypted tunnel, with mTLS enforced at the node level before any traffic reaches a workload.

For services requiring L7 capabilities (HTTP routing, JWT validation, header mutation), Waypoint proxies are deployed per-namespace or per-service account — full Envoy instances deployed on-demand rather than universally. L4 authorization policies are enforced directly by the ztunnel using SPIFFE SVIDs from L2.

ztunnel DaemonSet HBONE Tunneling Waypoint Proxies L4 mTLS Enforcement Envoy L7 Gateways Peer Authorization Policies
L2

Zero-Trust Identity Layer

IDENTITY & CERTIFICATES

SPIFFE / SPIRE (Secure Production Identity Framework For Everyone / SPIFFE Runtime Environment) issues every workload a cryptographically verifiable identity the moment it starts. There are no long-lived passwords, no static API keys, no service account JSON files. Each workload receives an X.509 SVID — a short-lived certificate encoding its SPIFFE URI (e.g. spiffe://orcawolf.mesh/ns/ehr/sa/fhir-gateway).

Certificate rotation is handled automatically by cert-manager, integrated with SPIRE's SVID TTL to renew before expiry — transparently, with zero downtime. Human operators authenticate via Workload Identity Federation, binding Google Cloud identities to mesh RBAC roles through OIDC token exchange.

SPIFFE / SPIRE Server X.509 SVIDs cert-manager Rotation Node Attestation Peer Authentication Workload Identity Federation
L3

EHR Interop + Data Sovereignty

HEALTH DATA LAYER

The FHIR R4 API gateway is the canonical interface for all Protected Health Information (PHI) exchange. Every FHIR request is validated against the requester's SPIFFE identity before routing begins. The HL7v2 bridge translates legacy HL7 v2.x messages (ADT feeds, lab results, pharmacy orders) into FHIR R4 resources in real time.

PHI sovereignty is enforced through CMEK at rest (L0), mTLS in transit (L1), and a data provenance ledger recording every read/write/transform event — each entry signed by the workload's SVID — creating an immutable audit chain satisfying HIPAA requirements natively. The de-identification pipeline uses the Cloud Healthcare API to produce Safe Harbor compliant datasets before any AI workload sees the data.

FHIR R4 Gateway HL7v2 Bridge US Core IG Profiles Data Provenance Ledger Cloud Healthcare API PHI De-identification
L4

AI Inference & Analytics

INTELLIGENCE LAYER

Vertex AI hosts clinical NLP models trained on de-identified FHIR corpora. The text-embedding-004 model converts clinical summaries into 768-dimensional semantic vectors — enabling cosine similarity search across historical cases without exposing raw PHI. Gemini provides multi-step clinical reasoning, synthesising structured FHIR data with unstructured clinical notes.

BigQuery provides the analytics substrate — petabyte-scale querying of de-identified clinical datasets with column-level access controls enforced by the mesh. All inference requests are authenticated with the calling workload's SVID, and results are logged to the provenance ledger at L3.

Vertex AI text-embedding-004 Gemini Reasoning BigQuery Analytics Clinical NLP Vector Similarity Search
L5

Observability & Compliance

TELEMETRY & AUDIT

Cloud Logging captures every mesh event in an immutable, tamper-evident log stream. Cloud Monitoring and Grafana dashboards provide real-time visibility into mesh health, certificate expiry, policy violations, and AI inference latency. Cloud Trace provides distributed request tracing across every hop in the mesh — from the FHIR gateway through de-identification to AI inference and back.

Compliance reporting is automated: HIPAA audit reports, NIST 800-53 control evidence, and FedRAMP continuous monitoring data are generated directly from the mesh telemetry stream — no manual evidence collection required.

Cloud Logging (Immutable) Grafana Dashboards Cloud Trace Prometheus Metrics HIPAA Audit Reports NIST 800-53 Controls
SECTION 04

Mass Casualty Incident (MCI) Simulation

The MCI Simulation engine provides a fully configurable, AI-driven triage and resource allocation tool for Mass Casualty Incidents — producing real FHIR R4 clinical bundles and a persistent exercise history.

4.1 How to Run a Simulation

  1. 1
    Select a scenario type

    Choose from: Blast / Explosion, Chemical / CBRN Exposure, Mass Trauma, Active Shooter, Natural Disaster, or Combined Arms. Each scenario applies different casualty probability weights based on published doctrine.

  2. 2
    Enter your incident parameters

    Provide location, total casualty count (1–5,000), available medical personnel, and transport assets.

  3. 3
    Hit "Run Simulation"

    The triage engine distributes casualties into RED (Immediate), YELLOW (Delayed), GREEN (Minimal), and BLACK (Expectant) categories, generates a timestamped event log, and produces a FHIR R4 Bundle.

  4. 4
    Download the FHIR Bundle

    Click "Download JSON" to save the generated bundle. This file can be loaded directly into fhir_mongo_loader.py or fed into the Vertex AI vector pipeline.

4.2 Triage Category Definitions (START / SALT Protocol)

TagCategoryDefinitionTreatment Priority
REDImmediateLife-threatening injuries survivable with immediate interventionHighest — treat within 60 minutes
YELLOWDelayedSerious injuries stable enough to wait for treatmentSecond — treat within 4–6 hours
GREENMinimalMinor injuries; walking wounded able to self-careThird — treat after RED and YELLOW
BLACKExpectantInjuries incompatible with survival given available resourcesComfort care only

4.3 Production Engine Integration

The simulation is backed by three production-grade Python components available in the simulation-engine/ directory of the GitHub repository:

  • fhir_mongo_loader.py — Loads generated FHIR Bundle JSON into MongoDB collections, routing each resource type (Patient, Condition, Observation) to its own collection with upsert logic to prevent duplicates.
  • fhir_vector_pipeline.py — Converts FHIR resources to semantic text summaries and generates 768-dimensional embeddings using Vertex AI text-embedding-004, enabling cosine similarity triage ranking.
  • locustfile.py — Locust-based load testing script that simulates concurrent CombatMedicUser agents submitting FHIR trauma records to the triage API endpoint.
✓
Every run is saved

All simulation runs are stored with their full FHIR bundle, triage breakdown, and a 768-dimensional semantic embedding vector for longitudinal analysis and scenario comparison.

SECTION 05

Carrier Readiness & C2 Dashboard

The Carrier Readiness simulation provides a Command and Control dashboard for medical and line-of-duty readiness across USS Nimitz (CVN-68) and USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) under multi-vector threat scenarios.

5.1 Calibration Settings

Click the ⚙ Calibration Settings button at the top of the page to open the four-tab mission configuration panel. All settings persist between sessions automatically.

TabWhat You Configure
Force ReadinessManning levels per role (Pilots, Navigators, Medical Personnel, Firemen, Weapon Operations, Deck Flight Crew) for each vessel; minimum viable thresholds for all readiness metrics.
Blood SupplyUnits on hand by blood product type. A red alert fires automatically when O-Negative falls below the 80-unit MASCAL minimum.
MedEvac AssetsAircraft and transport counts: MH-60S Seahawk, CH-53E Super Stallion, C-130 Hercules, C-17 Globemaster, LCU, and RHIB. Total lift capacity is calculated and displayed in real time.
Theater & EchelonSelect operational theater (Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea, Persian Gulf, Yemen Coast, South China Sea, Eastern Mediterranean, or custom coordinates). Interactive Leaflet map shows carrier position, 200nm CASEVAC radius ring, and Role 2–4 echelon markers.

5.2 Running an Exercise

  1. 1
    Select vessels

    Choose CVN-68, CVN-71, or both for a side-by-side comparison.

  2. 2
    Set crew complement

    From Command Element Only (500) up to Full Complement (6,000). Default is 6,000.

  3. 3
    Select threat scenario & intensity

    Drone Swarm, Sea-Skimming Missile, EW/GPS Denial, CBRN Exposure, or Combined Arms. Drag the intensity slider 1–100%.

  4. 4
    Hit "Run Exercise"

    Medical and LOD readiness dials update with colour-coded status (green / amber / red), the C2 event log streams line by line, and a Recommended Course of Action appears automatically.

  5. 5
    Print C2 Brief

    Click "⎙ Print C2 Brief" on any vessel panel to generate a print-ready classified-style brief — UNCLASSIFIED // FOR EXERCISE USE ONLY header, full metrics table, threshold status, and complete event log.

5.3 Reading the Dials

GREEN

Above Threshold — Mission Ready

Metric is above the minimum viable threshold. Full operational capability for this domain.

AMBER

Caution Zone — Monitor Closely

Metric is approaching the minimum viable threshold. Recommend pre-emptive resupply or redistribution.

RED

Below Threshold — Action Required

Metric has fallen below the configured minimum viable threshold. Immediate command action required per the Recommended COA.

DIAL VALUE

Reading the Number

The number displayed in each dial is the current readiness percentage for that metric, calculated from manning, supply levels, and threat degradation.

5.6 Recommended Course of Action

After every exercise run, the system automatically generates a prioritised action list modelled on standard operational reporting:

  • P1 Actions (red — immediate) — life-safety and mission-critical shortfalls requiring action within the current watch
  • P2 Actions (amber — urgent) — significant degradation requiring action within 24 hours
  • P3 Actions (green — routine) — monitoring and pre-emptive measures to sustain current readiness

The top-line recommendation tells the Commanding Officer whether to Maintain Tempo, Restrict Operations, or Withdraw / Request Relief based on the aggregate readiness score.

SECTION 06

Sovereign Mesh C2 — NATS JetStream Dashboard

The Mesh C2 Dashboard simulates a NATS JetStream edge telemetry feed from both carriers — streaming live MASCAL impacts, TBI exposures, and RTD clearances as JSON events on the mesh topic hierarchy.

6.1 What You're Seeing

The dashboard auto-starts on load. Every 1.8 seconds, a synthetic event fires on one of the six lines of duty across either vessel:

  • MASCAL_IMPACT (red) — kinetic strike causes casualties; combat effectiveness decreases; capacity bar drops
  • BLAST_EXPOSURE_DETECTED (amber) — overpressure exposure detected; TBI watch count increments; personnel remain on duty but are flagged for monitoring
  • RTD_CLEARED (green) — Return to Duty cleared; previously injured personnel restored to effective strength

6.2 NATS Topic Hierarchy

# Topic format: mesh.triage.{vessel}.{role}.{event_flag}
mesh.triage.cvn68.pilots.MASCAL_IMPACT
mesh.triage.cvn71.medicalpersonnel.BLAST_EXPOSURE_DETECTED
mesh.triage.cvn68.deckflightcrewmen.RTD_CLEARED

6.3 Live Link to Carrier Readiness

When both the Mesh C2 Dashboard and the Carrier Readiness page are open simultaneously, events from the C2 dashboard drive the Carrier Readiness telemetry feed in real time — the two dashboards form a connected C2 system, mirroring what a real NATS JetStream edge mesh would deliver to a ship's medical operations centre.

SECTION 07

Combat Medic Load Hammer

The Load Hammer simulates up to 50 concurrent CombatMedicUser agents submitting FHIR trauma records to the triage API — mirroring the behaviour of your Locust load testing script in a live browser environment.

7.1 How to Use It

  1. 1
    Set GCP Project ID

    Enter your Google Cloud project ID in the configuration panel at the top. This tags all simulated requests with your project context.

  2. 2
    Drag the agent slider

    Set the number of concurrent CombatMedicUser agents (1–50). Start with 10 to observe baseline behaviour, then scale up.

  3. 3
    Hit "Launch Hammer"

    Agents begin firing POST requests every 1–5 seconds with weighted random FHIR R4 trauma payloads across five scenario types.

  4. 4
    Click any request row

    Expands to show the full Vertex AI pipeline: clinical semantic summary, first 8 embedding dimensions, and cosine triage priority score.

7.2 Reading the Dashboard

8.1 How the Workflow Diagrams Work

Each of the six tracks is drawn as a left-to-right workflow: an input, four clickable steps, then an output. Hover over a track and the connecting lines animate. Click any step to open a panel showing what it does, where its data comes from, what it produces, and live figures with a table or chart built from the runs saved on the site.

Reading the badges. Computed from your runs means the figures come from simulations saved on the MCI Simulation and Carrier Readiness pages. Illustrative reference means a reference design (for example the Argo CD and policy examples) that is not connected to a live cluster.

8.2 How to Demo This Page (5-Minute Script)

Open the one-page printable cheat sheet →

  1. 1
    Prepare (before the meeting). Run three or four simulations on the MCI Simulation page (try Blast, Chemical and Active Shooter) and two or three exercises on the Carrier Readiness page. The Innovation panels then show your own saved results. With no saved runs, the page falls back to clearly labelled reference scenarios.

    Open with the banner (30 sec). Point to the top of the page: all figures are synthetic training data with no operational feeds. Say this first — it sets the right expectation.

Change the scenario and the responders-on-scene control live to show the shortfall move.

    Show Resource Modeling (30 sec). It turns the forecast into a responder count — “how many people do we need”.
  5. 5
    Pick one governance track (1 min). Open Ambient Mesh GitOps or Sovereign Data Mesh to show policy-as-code and data ownership, and call out the “Illustrative reference” badge honestly.
  6. 6
    Close with the Outcome-Driven Resource Optimizer (1 min). Show the Gemini reasoning step and note it is a template-written brief, not a live model call.

SECTION 13

Glossary of Terms

Ambient Mesh
Istio architecture mode that eliminates per-pod sidecar proxies, moving L4 enforcement to per-node ztunnel agents.
CASEVAC
Casualty Evacuation — movement of casualties from point of injury to a higher echelon of medical care.
CBRN
Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear — threat classification for non-conventional weapons.
CMEK
Customer-Managed Encryption Key — encryption key held and controlled by the customer, not the cloud provider.
COA
Course of Action — a recommended set of actions for a commander to address a tactical situation.
EMCON
Emissions Control — operational state controlling radio and radar emissions to reduce detection signature.
FHIR R4
Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources Release 4 — the modern HL7 standard for clinical data exchange via REST APIs.
GKE
Google Kubernetes Engine — Google's managed Kubernetes service.
HBONE
HTTP-Based Overlay Network Encapsulation — the tunneling protocol used by Istio Ambient Mesh ztunnel for encrypted inter-node traffic.
HL7 v2
Health Level Seven Version 2 — the legacy message-based healthcare data standard used by most existing hospital systems.
JOMIS
Joint Operational Medical Information System — DoD programme for theatre medical command and control.
MASCAL
Mass Casualty — a military medical term for an incident producing more casualties than available resources can immediately treat.
MEDEVAC
Medical Evacuation — movement of casualties using dedicated medical transport assets with en-route care.
mTLS
Mutual Transport Layer Security — TLS where both client and server authenticate with certificates before communication.
MVT
Minimum Viable Threshold — the floor readiness percentage below which a metric triggers a command action.
NATS JetStream
NATS is a high-performance messaging system; JetStream is its persistent streaming layer used for edge telemetry.
PHI
Protected Health Information — individually identifiable health data protected under HIPAA.
RTD
Return to Duty — medical clearance returning a casualty to full operational status.
SPIFFE
Secure Production Identity Framework For Everyone — open standard for workload identity in zero-trust environments.
SPIRE
SPIFFE Runtime Environment — the production implementation of the SPIFFE standard.
SVID
SPIFFE Verifiable Identity Document — a short-lived X.509 certificate encoding a workload's SPIFFE URI.
TCCC
Tactical Combat Casualty Care — US military field medicine protocol for combat casualty management.
TBI
Traumatic Brain Injury — blast overpressure injury requiring monitoring and removal from high-risk duty.
VPC-SC
VPC Service Controls — Google Cloud security perimeter preventing data exfiltration from a defined resource boundary.
Vertex AI
Google Cloud's managed machine learning platform for training, deploying, and serving AI models.
ztunnel
Zero-Trust Tunnel — the per-node agent in Istio Ambient Mesh responsible for L4 mTLS enforcement.
